content: The sample size of the study was small, and the optimal information size (OIS) was not achieved. The point estimate did not meet the pre-specified threshold for clinical importance, defined as a mean difference (MD) of -1. The confidence interval crossed the null value, with its lower and upper boundaries extending beyond the pre-specified thresholds for both appreciable benefit (MD = -1) and harm (MD = +1). The study did not exhibit significant inconsistency, as indicated by an I² value of 10%. This suggests a low level of statistical heterogeneity among the included trials. The study by Elserty (2016) included two arms: one comparing fixed pulse TENS combined with exercise versus exercise alone, and the other comparing adjusted pulse TENS combined with exercise versus exercise alone. Both arms were included in the meta-analysis by splitting the comparison group numbers in half. The trials were conducted in different countries, including lowand lower-middle-income settings, and no downgrading for indirectness was applied. However, the risk of bias was downgraded once due to potential selection, performance, and other biases. The study by Depaoli Lemos (2021) utilized four TENS sessions, while Petrofsky (2020) employed a single TENS session. The inconsistency in the findings was not downgraded, as the I² value was 4%, indicating minimal heterogeneity. The study by Koftolis and Jamison involved participants undergoing 20 to 90 treatment sessions. However, inconsistency was downgraded twice due to point estimates in different directions with little to no overlap in confidence intervals (I² = 94%), suggesting considerable heterogeneity that could not be explained by small subgroups. Imprecision was downgraded once due to the small sample size, as the OIS was not reached. The point estimate did not meet the threshold for clinical importance (MD = -1), and the confidence interval crossed the null value. The study by Petrofsky (2020) included four arms, comparing various combinations of continuous TENS, sham heat, and low-level continuous heat. All arms were included in the meta-analysis by appropriately splitting the comparison group numbers. The inconsistency was not downgraded in some cases, as the I² value was low (e.g., 28%). However, in other cases, inconsistency was downgraded once or twice due to differences in the magnitude and direction of point estimates, with some overlap in confidence intervals (e.g., I² = 65% or 69%). Imprecision was downgraded twice in some studies due to small sample sizes and confidence intervals crossing the null value. In other cases, imprecision was downgraded once for similar reasons. The study by Depaoli Lemos (2021) used four TENS sessions, while other studies varied in the number of sessions and treatment protocols. The inconsistency in findings was downgraded twice in some cases due to point estimates in different directions and little to no overlap in confidence intervals (e.g., I² = 97%). Overall, the evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework, considering factors such as risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias. The findings were used to inform the WHO guideline on the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults.
